intention: A serial token-passing protocol for device maintenance cycles. When the system is idle, the cairn device starts a sleep-cycle token on its announce feed. Every device's probe fires on that message; the device whose turn it is in alpha order (from the ground loop's roster) either runs its sleep cycle and forwards the token, or just forwards immediately if it has no sleep work. The probe is the pattern, not a class — a three-line custom probe (match, decide, forward) is a valid implementation; no shim overhead, no bus routing, no LLM needed. Serial execution is the day-one shape because of measured OOM history (n=3) and because we don't yet know which sleep cycles are independent — parallel is a measured refinement for later.
why: Many devices need periodic maintenance — consolidation, learning, question processing, false-positive improvement (the 'overnight run' from the origin idea). Without coordination, N independent maintenance daemons compete for resources (the OOM history) and provide no ordering guarantees. One token rotation replaces N independent sleep daemons — the same move the ground loop made for heartbeats. The idle detection is the '3 hours without a human' screensaver-like trigger Akien named: 'it's not about a specific hour, it's about when other external things won't trouble it.'
traces_to: Telos aim 5 (self-improving) — sleep cycles are where learning consolidation and question processing happen. Telos aim 1 (inference compilation) — consolidation compiles accumulated evidence into structure, which is Law 1 at a batch scale. The shrinking-footprint derivation (event-not-poll): one token rotation vs N independent daemons. Law 4 — the token is physics (a message on the bus), not policy (a rule about who runs when).
gates: code-seam invariants: proved (tester seal, teeth a hollow build could not pass) + feeds back to origin on failure. Dependency: the cairn device must be built (devices/cairn/ with announce-feed capability) before BUILDME can proceed. WATCHME(sleep-rotation-completes): emission gate resolves ARMED from the probe path before the crossing. Children prove first.
falsifier: Done-tell: the cairn device can start a sleep token, at least one device can receive and forward it, and the rotation completes back to start with at least one real sleep cycle executed. Wrong-intent tell: devices need to run their maintenance concurrently (measured, not assumed), the idle detection is better located elsewhere than the cairn device, or the token-passing overhead exceeds independent device-level scheduling.
horizon: First end-to-end rotation is the first measurement. Three rotations with real sleep work is the watch's enough.
children: idle-detection-trigger — the '3 hours without a human' screensaver-like trigger on the cairn device. Code-seam at devices/cairn/.
token-rotation-mechanism — token posting on the announce feed, per-device probe pattern, alpha-order forwarding, and cycle completion detection. Code-seam at devices/cairn/.
dependencies: The cairn device (I-the-cairn-device) must be built — devices/cairn/ does not exist yet. The bus (built and proven). The ground loop roster (built and proven). The probe pattern (tools/base/probe.py, built and proven).
distinctions_recorded: No separate subscription registry — the rotation is the full alpha device list from the ground loop roster. Every device's probe fires; non-sleeping devices just forward. Settled in conversation: an active 'pass' is just the probe shape (message present → is for us? → no, done; yes → do we sleep? → no → forward), not a poll.

The probe is a design pattern, not a class — a three-line custom probe that matches, decides, and forwards is valid. No shim, no bus routing, no LLM. 'When we were first talking about probes you were trying to give them LLM access, and then it was a complex schema thing' (Akien, 2026-08-24). The base probe covers most things; a custom probe is equally allowed.
Serial by design, parallel deferred to measurement. The OOM history (n=3) and not knowing which cycles are independent settle this for day one.

Held-out devices (those benched by the heartbeat) are not special-cased — their probe fires like anyone else's. If the device is held out, its shim still receives the token and forwards it. The heartbeat's bench is about probes, not about bus messages.
